title: Pulse capacity reserve & price-trigger playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick runnable playbook and compact sheet to allocate short-term reserve capacity, adjust headcount/contractor mix for a 6-10 week sprint window, and define pricing triggers that are safe for customers and preserve runway. Idea: small, automated reserve + price-trigger ladder to avoid big layoffs or surprise margin collapses during token-price compression windows.

Executive summary (2 lines):
- Create a 6-week pulse reserve (GPU-hour bucket + contractor pool) sized to cover 30% of highest observed 7-day throughput spikes; finance funds from ops buffer.
- Implement three-tiered price trigger system (soft nudge, partial-slab, emergency-slab) tied to 7-day realized unit cost and committed capacity utilization; each trigger maps to specific headcount/contractor actions.

Key assumptions (named):
- AVG_TOKEN_COST_HOSTED = $0.00006 per token (current blended cost across regions).
- HIGH_SPike_MULTIPLIER = 2.4x baseline 7-day usage when a viral customer event occurs.
- CONTRACTOR_LOAD_FACTOR = 0.6 (contractor effective output compared to FTE).
- RESERVE_GPU_HOURS_UNIT = 32 hours per reserved GPU per week (assumes 8h warm/busy window).

Scenario matrix (Apr-Jun 2026) - simplified 3-scenario view:
Columns: Scenario | Avg daily tokens (M) | 7d peak tokens (M) | Monthly revenue ($k) | Monthly infra cost ($k) | FTEs (prod/infra/ops) | Temp contractors | Reserve GPU hrs/week | Price_per_1k_tokens ($)
Baseline | 75 | 100 | 1,980 | 550 | 42 / 18 / 12 | 8 contractors | 192 | 0.80
Demand-spike | 120 | 288 | 3,168 | 1,360 | 42 / 18 / 12 | 20 contractors | 384 | 0.95
Price-compression | 60 | 90 | 1,584 | 420 | 40 / 16 / 11 | 6 contractors | 128 | 0.70

Notes on matrix: revenue numbers use blended take-rate and assumed product mix; infra cost includes GPU, storage, egress and 15% overhead. Reserve GPU hours/week is target for the pulse reserve (multiple GPUs reserved but not always active).

Headcount flex plan (6-week sprint):
- Week 0: spin up contractor bench: 10 short-term infra/devops contractors (4-week terms with option to extend), budget = $128k total (labor + onboarding).
- Week 1-2: measure 7-day rolling peak; if peak > 1.8x baseline, shift 40% of non-critical infra tasks to contractors; freeze non-essential hiring.
- Week 3-4: if price-trigger Tier 2 (partial-slab) fires, temporarily reassign 1 product PM and 2 engineers to customer-critical triage; defer 1 planned hire.
- Week 5-6: post-sprint review; either ramp down contractors (preferred) or convert highest-performing contractor to 6-month FT temp (only if sustained demand).

Price-trigger ladder (automated rules):
- Tier 0 (monitor): 7d realized unit cost between 0.9x and 1.1x baseline. Action: no change, notify finance + SRE.
- Tier 1 (soft nudge): 7d realized unit cost > 1.2x baseline OR reserve utilization > 50% for 48h. Action: enable minor price nudge (+10% on new non-committed customers for next 7 days), throttle burst allocations for non-critical customers.
- Tier 2 (partial-slab): 7d realized unit cost > 1.5x baseline OR sustained 72h reserve utilization > 70%. Action: enable partial slab on slab-eligible accounts (apply 20% incremental price for excess tokens above committed slabs), shift traffic to cheaper model variants where quality acceptable, notify sales to contact top-tier customers.
- Tier 3 (emergency slab): 7d realized unit cost > 2.0x baseline OR sustained 96h reserve utilization > 85%. Action: emergency pricing corridor (+40% on burst), auto-fallback to lower-cost model family for non-enterprise tiers, apply hard rate limits for new signups, activate emergency hiring/contractor surge budget.

Risk & customer impact notes:
- Soft nudges should be tested on a 5% customer sample to ensure retention signals are not strongly negative.
- Enterprise commitments should be excluded from auto-hard limits; instead use negotiated fallback/offload play (regional routing to Dedicated pools or scheduled maintenance windows).

Cost math highlights (quick check):
- If reserve = 4x v100-equivalent GPUs at 32 hrs/week = 4 * 32 = 128 hrs/week. If per-GPU reserved cost (amortized) = $6.5/hr, weekly reserve = $832, monthly ~ $3.3k - this is illustrative; blended infra cost per token drives trigger thresholds instead.
- Contractor budgeting: assume blended contractor fully-burdened rate = $90/hr; 10 contractors * 120 hrs/mo => $108k/mo including 20% onboarding overhead ~ $129.6k.

Operational checklist (immediate actions):
1) Finance: allocate $150k pulse reserve fund from ops buffer and create a distinct GL bucket (target: cover contractor + reserved GPU for 6 weeks). Owner: Aisha. Deadline: 2026-03-15.
2) SRE/Infra: create reserve project with 4 pre-warmed GPUs in us-west and eu-west, expose utilization telemetry to finance dashboard. Owner: Evan. Deadline: 2026-03-12.
3) Product/PM: draft comms template for soft nudge and partial-slab customers; legal review on price change language. Owner: Sofia. Deadline: 2026-03-18.
4) Sales/CS: prepare enterprise playbook for negotiated fallbacks (do not apply auto-hard limits to committed customers). Owner: Ethan V. (CS lead). Deadline: 2026-03-20.

Metrics to track (dashboards to add):
- 7d realized unit cost (blended), 1h/24h/7d windows
- Reserve utilization (per region)
- % new signups affected by soft nudge
- Net churn within 14 days of price nudge (cohort)
- Contractor throughput vs FTE baseline (weekly)

Decision points & escalation ladder:
- If Tier 2 triggers persist for >14 days => escalate to CEO+CFO+CTO for possible contract renegotiation or short-term top-line measures.
- If Tier 3 triggers fire => exec emergency review within 48h (consider temporary product gating and sales credits).

Open questions / follow-ups (notes to self):
- Need a clear definition of "realized unit cost" (include fixed infra amortization vs marginal GPU cost). Confluence draft ID linked.
- Test plan for price-nudge cohort A/B experiment: sample selection, guardrails, rollback criteria.
- Legal sign-off on auto-pricing language for EU customers.

Appendix (quick sheet rows you can paste into a spreadsheet):
Row headers: metric, formula/assumption, baseline, notes
1) Baseline token unit cost, = infra_cost / tokens => 0.00006, derived from Feb blended data
2) Reserve buffer target, = max(0.3 * 7d_peak_tokens, baseline weeks 3*avg_daily_tokens) => variable
3) Contractor hourly rate, = 90 => blended assumed
4) Conversion factor FTE->contractor, = 0.6 => used for planning

Next steps (who to ping now):
- Ping SRE slack #infra-cost-ops for telemetry wiring (Evan).
- Set a 30-min sync (finance + product + infra + sales) next Tue to rubber-stamp triggers and timeline.

Raw quick notes / scratch (for revision):
- Consider adding a mid-sprint micro-discount for high-volume customers who opt-in to model-fallback routing (helps retention while reducing marginal cost).
- Evaluate whether Dedicated customers in eu-west can be used as controlled spillover for hosted overloads (contractual permitting).
- Keep a 10% minimum ops buffer uncommitted for unforeseen legal or compliance charges.

Document history: initial draft 2026-01-20 by Aisha Malik; collaborator edits 2026-02-12 (Evan) and 2026-03-10 (Sofia); flagged for exec review after pilot.
